FILE TRUST & VERIFICATION

Check files.
Verify trust.

A shared file-verification layer for games and applications. VDSP fingerprints files, checks reputation, and sends uploads to an isolated server-side scanning pipeline. Results are evidence—not a promise that a file is harmless.

Scan a fileDeveloper portal ↗
Workflow

From file to evidence

Each stage has a clear job. The browser never executes the file, and a clean scan alone never grants VDSP approval.

01 / LOCALChoose a file

Check size and calculate its SHA-256 fingerprint in the browser.

02 / IDENTITYAuthenticate

Use Firebase sign-in or a server-only API key with scan permission.

03 / ANALYSISScan in isolation

Inspect type, hash reputation and configured malware scanner output.

04 / DECISIONReturn evidence

Report approved, unverified or blacklisted only when the required evidence exists.

Public tool

Check a file

Calculate the file hash locally, then optionally submit it to your configured VDSP API. Don't upload confidential files unless you own them and understand your server's retention policy.

File analysis

Browser pre-check runs locally. Server scanning requires a configured HTTPS API.

Never paste a secret API key into this page. The browser can use a Firebase user token; permanent developer API keys are for trusted servers only.

Trust levels

A file is never approved only because one scanner found no threat.

VDSP ApprovedExact hash, valid signature and trusted review evidence match.
VDSP UnverifiedPending, unsupported, not scanned, scan error or no trusted approval.
VDSP BlacklistedExact hash is blocked or a configured scanner reports a detection.
Browser checks are limited. The API must use HTTPS, validate identity, isolate uploads and never execute submitted files.

Create an account to receive a Creator ID and issue or revoke server-side API keys. Your API key is shown only once when created. A public App ID can go in client code; a secret API key must stay on a trusted server.

Account access

Account identity is handled by Firebase Authentication. Never share your password, service-account file or secret API key.

Integration

Built for game and app developers

Integrate through an HTTPS API from a trusted backend, or use Firebase Authentication for user-facing clients. Do not embed permanent secret credentials in downloadable clients.

⌘

Creator ID & App ID

Stable identifiers for the developer and the application. These identify an integration; they do not grant privileged access.

Public identifiers
⚿

Server API key

Scoped credential for trusted servers. Stored as a hash on the API side, shown once on creation, and revocable.

Secret · server only
✓

File fingerprint

SHA-256 ties a result to exact bytes. A changed file gets a different fingerprint and must be checked again.

SHA-256

Example request

Run this on your trusted backend, never inside a public client.

curl -X POST "$VDSP_API/v1/scan" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VDSP_SERVER_API_KEY" \
  -F "file=@./your-file.zip"

Example response

A scan without trusted approval stays unverified.

{
  "fileId": "...",
  "sha256": "...",
  "status": "unverified",
  "scanStatus": "no_detection",
  "signatureStatus": "not_checked"
}

See the package's docs/API.md for all current endpoints and deployment requirements.

Help center

Common questions

Where do I get my Creator ID?

Create an account in the Developer Portal, verify your email, then sign in. The API creates your Creator profile and displays the Creator ID in your dashboard.

Where do I get my API key?

After email verification and sign-in, choose Generate API key. It is displayed only once. If lost, revoke it and create a new one; the server cannot reveal the old secret.

Can I put the API key in my game's code?

Not if the game is distributed to other people. They can inspect the client and extract the secret. Use a public App ID in the client and route privileged requests through your own server, or use Firebase Authentication and short-lived user tokens.

Does “no detection” mean safe?

No. Scanners can miss threats. VDSP approval requires exact-file identity, a valid signature and trusted review evidence. Unknown or failed scans remain unverified.

Does Firebase scan files for malware?

No. Firebase stores identity and records. The VDSP API must run a configured scanning engine, such as ClamAV, in an isolated environment.
